name: Naturalisation

requirements.blocker_text: Requires at least 8 years' residence in Estonia in total.
requirements.fix_path: Accumulate at least 8 years of residence in Estonia.

requirements.blocker_text: Requires at least the last 5 years of that residence to be on a permanent basis immediately preceding the application, held under a long-term residence permit or the right of permanent residence.
Requires passing the Estonian language proficiency examination at B1, unless exempt (education completed in Estonian).
requirements.fix_path: Pass the Estonian language proficiency examination at B1.

requirements.blocker_text: Requires passing an examination on the Estonian Constitution and the Citizenship Act.
requirements.fix_path: Book and pass the Constitution and Citizenship Act examination.

requirements.blocker_text: Requires demonstrating loyalty to the Estonian state.

evidence_required.document: Proof of 8 years' total and 5 years' immediately-preceding residence
Estonian language proficiency certificate (or exemption evidence)
Constitution and Citizenship Act examination pass certificate
Registered place of residence in Estonia's Population Register

sources.title: Police and Border Guard Board of Estonia (politsei.ee) -- Estonian citizenship for an adult: conditions

notes: NEW ROUTE, part of Estonia's initial build. prerequisites points to ee_long_term_resident because the source explicitly requires the residence to be held 'on the basis of a long-term residence permit or the right of permanent residence' -- unlike Barbados, where the equivalent link was not confirmed and left null. dual_citizenship_allowed is left null rather than guessed: Estonia's general rule (via the Ministry of the Interior's citizenship overview) was not resolved to a clear tier-1 statement on whether a second, non-EU nationality may be retained -- multiple tier-3 sources describe a historically restrictive stance with a narrower reform track, not independently confirmed here. The 96-month (8-year) and 60-month (5-year continuous) tests are modelled as two separate hard requirements within the same group (both AND-required), rather than one combined figure, to keep each one individually traceable to its own blocker/fix_path.
